notes: Five of the six records a round-54 agent returned on the moves row. Singapore was HELD, not filed, for two reasons recorded in the research log: the only full statutory text the agent could open was the lawplayer.com consolidation rather than Singapore Statutes Online, and more importantly section 11A, the President's discretion to refuse or revoke the appointment of the chairperson, directors or managing director, is in Singapore a constitutional safeguard held by the Elected President against the elected government, so citing it as the state controlling the bank inverts what it is for. Of the remaining provisions the agent found, the ministerial final say on a primary dealer's appeal (section 149) and the Minister's directions over the Financial Sector Development Fund (section 127) are an ordinary administrative appeal right and a fund mandate, a long way from the Kuwait record where the Minister of Finance's directives bind the bank. Singapore stays absent on this row. Taiwan's summary was tightened: the source states where the institution sits in the machinery of government and does not say the cabinet decides monetary policy, so the record now says that rather than implying the policy power moved.

records.kind: central bank law put under government-ordered review
records.summary: Treasurer Ian Ling-Stuckey, acting in consultation with the Prime Minister and the Ministerial Economic Committee of the National Executive Council, issued terms of reference dated 13 May 2021 for a review of the Central Banking Act 2000 that was directed to examine whether the Bank of Papua New Guinea Governor should keep his sole power to determine monetary policy under section 10, and to reassess the governance arrangements and the length of senior management terms at the Bank.
records.source_title: Review of the Central Banking Act 2000, Phase One Report - Annex 1: Terms of Reference

records.kind: statutory arrangement placing the central bank under the cabinet
records.summary: Under the revised Central Bank of China Act promulgated on 8 November 1979, Taiwan's central bank sits as a state bank and an agency under the Executive Yuan, the cabinet, rather than standing outside the executive branch; the bank's own official history records that it has been under the Executive Yuan since that reorganisation, having previously been under the Presidential Office. What the source states is where the institution sits in the machinery of government. It does not say the cabinet decides monetary policy, and the Act leaves rate and policy decisions with the bank's own board, so this is the organisational form of the arrangement rather than a transfer of the policy power. It is a standing arrangement with no end date and no episode attached.
records.source_title: Brief History - Central Bank of the Republic of China (Taiwan)

records.kind: statutory arrangement removing the bank's control of monetary policy
records.summary: Decree-Law 361 of 2018, issued by Cuba's Council of State and published in the Gaceta Oficial on 12 October 2018 in place of Decree-Law 172 of 1997, strips the Banco Central de Cuba of autonomy over monetary policy by requiring the bank to design monetary policy in coordination with the government's fiscal and macroeconomic objectives under an annual policy agreement signed by ministers. This is a standing arrangement with no end date and no episode attached.
records.source_title: New Financial Regulations in Cuba: Less Autonomy for Monetary Policy and More Space for Foreign Capital and Microcredit

records.kind: statutory arrangement giving the cabinet power over the central bank
records.summary: Decretal Federal Law No. 14 of 2018 places the Central Bank of the UAE under the federal Cabinet in several respects at once: board members are appointed by federal decree on the Cabinet's recommendation (Article 11) and their membership may be terminated by federal decree on the Cabinet's approval (Article 14), the exchange rate regime is set only on a board proposal with Cabinet approval (Article 31), and the bank may not withdraw a currency denomination from circulation without Cabinet approval (Article 59). This is a standing arrangement with no end date and no episode attached.
records.source_title: Decretal Federal Law No. (14) of 2018 Regarding the Central Bank and Organization of Financial Institutions and Activities

records.kind: statutory arrangement putting the government in charge of the central bank
records.summary: The Law on the National Bank of the Lao PDR, approved by the National Assembly on 14 October 1995 and promulgated by Presidential Decree No. 29, puts the government at the head of the central bank. Article 11 makes a Deputy Prime Minister the chairman of the bank's Board of Management, with the Governor and the Minister of Finance as vice-chairs. Article 12 has board members appointed or removed by the Prime Minister, on the Governor's proposal. Under Article 19 the Governor researches monetary, interest rate and exchange rate policy and proposes it to the Board of Management, and then submits it to the Government, which considers it and decides whether to adopt, promulgate and implement it, so the final decision rests with the Government rather than the bank. This is a standing arrangement with no end date and no episode attached.
records.source_title: Law on the National Bank of the Lao PDR, No. 05/95/NA (Lao Official Gazette)
